cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exercise 2, ch. XIII] On 1 March Dionysos' slave Lukas (PECULIUM) buys a ton of grain from Verres, who mistakenly believes it to be his (it belongs to Turia), and receives the keys to the locked warehouse in Ostia. On 1 April Lukas takes the grain to his master's mill, where it is ground. Two weeks later Turia demands it back. Legal situation?
cards.back:
• Possession: Verres possesses; Dionysos acquires possession through Lukas (PECULIUM, ANIMO SERVORUM) — with the keys, if the warehouse is locked and they are the only means of access (Gaius D 41.1.9.6; not a symbolic delivery), at the latest with the removal on 1 April.
• Derivative acquisition of ownership: fails — Verres is neither owner nor authorised to dispose.
• USUCAPIO: RES HABILIS (Verres in good faith, no FURTUM), possession, BONA FIDES (Lukas knows nothing; Dionysos need not know of the purchase), causa: sale (slaves conclude contracts within the Peculium) — but TEMPUS (1 year) is lacking.
• Grinding = SPECIFICATIO? Flour is a new form, not a mere uncovering as with threshing → irreversible: Proculians/MEDIA SENTENTIA → Dionysos (in whose name the grain is ground) acquires originally; Turia: ACTIO IN FACTUM (good faith). Sabinians: Turia remains owner → REI VINDICATIO against Dionysos.
• With the new thing, the usucaption of the grain comes to an end.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exercise 2, Kap. XIII] Dionysos' Sklave Lukas (PECULIUM) kauft am 1.3. von Verres eine Tonne Getreide, die Verres irrig für seine hält (sie gehört Turia), und erhält die Schlüssel zum verschlossenen Speicher in Ostia. Am 1.4. bringt Lukas das Getreide in die Mühle seines Herrn, wo es gemahlen wird. Zwei Wochen später verlangt Turia es zurück. Rechtslage?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 1] Felix owes Gaia 1.000 and gives her his cow as a pledge. At maturity Gaia grants him a one-year respite and returns the cow for his use. Felix dies; his unsuspecting heir Hermes sells and delivers the cow to the bona fide Japyx, who slaughters it and makes sausages. (a) When/how does the right of pledge arise? (b) Effect of the return? (c) Of the inheritance? (d) Of the slaughtering/processing?
cards.back:
(a) With the CONVENTIO PIGNORIS: claim (1.000) + Felix's ownership + pledge agreement; the delivery additionally establishes the contract of pledge (possessory pledge).
(b) Return for use is not a waiver (waiver only with permission to alienate) → the right of pledge continues as a non-possessory one.
(c) Hermes steps into Felix's position (debt and burdened ownership). His sale without consent is not FURTUM (good faith, no DOLUS) → Japyx acquires ownership (cow = RES MANCIPI: bonitarian), but burdened with the right of pledge — it attaches to the thing.
(d) Slaughtering and sausage-making: the cow ceases to exist; sausages are an ALIUD (SPECIFICATIO) → the right of pledge terminates (cf Paulus (Cassius) D 13.7.18.3). Gaia is left with her personal claim against the heir Hermes.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 1] Felix schuldet Gaia 1.000 und gibt ihr seine Kuh als Pfand. Bei Fälligkeit stundet Gaia ein Jahr und gibt die Kuh zur Nutzung zurück. Felix stirbt; sein ahnungsloser Erbe Hermes verkauft und übergibt die Kuh an den gutgläubigen Japyx, der sie schlachtet und Würste macht. (a) Wann/wodurch entsteht das Pfandrecht? (b) Wirkung der Rückgabe? (c) der Erbschaft? (d) des Schlachtens/Verarbeitens?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 2] Without authority, Melitta sells Diana's ship (10.000; revenue 70/month) and cart (5.000; 50/month) to Leo. Diana's REI VINDICATIO begins on 1 May (LITIS CONTESTATIO). Leo uses the ship until 1 July, when it is struck by lightning and burns down. He leaves the cart unused in the barn and on 1 August saws it up into firewood (600). On 1 September Leo is condemned. Diana's claims (a) concerning the ship, (b) concerning the cart?
cards.back:
(a) Ship: fruits since LC (RESTITUERE): 2 × 70 = 140 (FRUCTUS PERCEPTI). Accidental destruction (CASUS) after LC: according to the Sabinians/Paulus (D 6.1.16.1: using the ship is not negligent) no liability for the value; according to the Proculians (RESTITUERE) liability even for accident → 10.000.
(b) Cart: FRUCTUS PERCIPIENDI for 4 months (1 May–1 September) = 200, although unused. Intentional destruction (DOLUS): liability on all views (fiction of possession, PRO POSSESSIONE DOLUS EST) → value 5.000 (on wilful refusal, assessment by IUSIURANDUM IN LITEM). The firewood belongs to Leo by irreversible SPECIFICATIO.
• Leo keeps fruits from before LC if he was in good faith.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 2] Melitta verkauft unbefugt Dianas Schiff (10.000; Ertrag 70/Monat) und Wagen (5.000; 50/Monat) an Leo. Dianas REI VINDICATIO beginnt am 1.5. (LITIS CONTESTATIO). Leo nutzt das Schiff bis 1.7., dann verbrennt es durch Blitzschlag. Den Wagen lässt er ungenutzt in der Scheune und zersägt ihn am 1.8. zu Brennholz (600). Am 1.9. wird Leo verurteilt. Ansprüche Dianas (a) wegen des Schiffs, (b) wegen des Wagens?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 4] Kreon owes Hekuba 500 and pledges his horse to her (non-possessory). With Hekuba's consent he sells it to Merops for 600; the proceeds, kept in a closed sack, are to be pledged to Hekuba, and Kreon takes the sack into his keeping. (a) Creation of the right of pledge, action? (b) Effect of the sale? (c) Kreon's unsuspecting heir Nastes pays bills with the coins. (d) What if Kreon had sold without Hekuba's consent?
cards.back:
(a) With the CONVENTIO PIGNORIS (claim + ownership + agreement; no delivery needed); from maturity VINDICATIO PIGNORIS (ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN REM).
(b) Unreserved consent = waiver → Merops acquires unburdened ownership. At the same time a new non-possessory right of pledge in the coins in the sack (new CONVENTIO PIGNORIS).
(c) Spending another's money in good faith: the recipients acquire ownership originally (NUMMOS CONSUMERE; no vindication against them) → the coins are practically lost for Hekuba's pledge; she retains the claim (500) against the heir Nastes (result derived from IX.D.2).
(d) Knowing alienation of a movable pledged thing without consent → Kreon is a FUR; Merops probably acquires no ownership (RES FURTIVA); Hekuba's pledge remains → VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against Merops, ACTIO FURTI against Kreon.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 4] Kreon schuldet Hekuba 500 und verpfändet ihr (besitzlos) sein Pferd. Mit Hekubas Zustimmung verkauft er es um 600 an Merops; der Erlös soll in einem verschlossenen Sack Hekuba verpfändet sein, Kreon verwahrt ihn. (a) Entstehung des Pfandrechts, Klage? (b) Wirkung des Verkaufs? (c) Kreons ahnungsloser Erbe Nastes zahlt mit den Münzen Rechnungen. (d) Was, wenn Kreon ohne Hekubas Zustimmung verkauft hätte?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 5] Merops leases an apple orchard from Felix. The ripe apples fall to the ground; Nastes secretly gathers them with larcenous intent, distils schnapps from them and sells and delivers it to the unsuspecting Leo. (a) Whose apples does Nastes appropriate? (b) Does Leo become owner of the schnapps? (c) What can the victim of the theft do?
cards.back:
(a) Felix's — upon separation (falling to the ground), fruits go to the owner of the mother object; the lessee Merops acquires only by PERCEPTIO.
(b) Yes — distilling schnapps is irreversible SPECIFICATIO → Nastes acquires ownership originally (even as a thief; bad faith changes nothing under property law). Leo acquires derivatively from the owner by purchase + delivery.
(c) Felix: vindication fails (apples no longer exist, schnapps belongs to Leo); against Nastes CONDICTIO FURTIVA (value) + ACTIO FURTI. Merops: ACTIO CONDUCTI against Felix (cf Example 26).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 5] Merops pachtet von Felix einen Apfelgarten. Die reifen Äpfel fallen zu Boden; Nastes sammelt sie heimlich in Diebstahlsabsicht, brennt daraus Schnaps und verkauft und übergibt diesen an den ahnungslosen Leo. (a) Wessen Äpfel eignet sich Nastes an? (b) Wird Leo Eigentümer des Schnapses? (c) Was kann der Bestohlene tun?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 6] Elektra has the tailor Juno make a dress from her silk (December). In February Juno sells the dress to Livia for 1.500 and deceives Elektra with a pretended theft. Livia dies in April; from May her unsuspecting heir Cleo keeps the dress in her wardrobe for over a year. In August of the following year Cleo sells and delivers it to Melitta for 250, who turns it into a patchwork rug in October. Possession and ownership in (a) January, (b) March, (c) July of the following year, (d) October?
cards.back:
(a) January: contract for work (LOCATIO CONDUCTIO OPERIS) → no SPECIFICATIO effect, ownership stays with Elektra, who commissioned the dress; Juno is detentor, Elektra mediate possessor.
(b) March: Juno sold the entrusted thing with intent to enrich herself → FURTUM (embezzlement); Livia is possessor; owner Elektra; dress = RES FURTIVA.
(c) July of the following year: Elektra remains owner — despite Cleo's good faith and more than a year of possession, no usucaption (LEX ATINIA).
(d) October: Melitta is possessor; by irreversible processing (rug) she acquires ownership originally (SPECIFICATIO — possible even with a stolen thing). Elektra: ACTIO IN FACTUM against Melitta (good faith); against Juno CONDICTIO FURTIVA + ACTIO FURTI.
• (The book mistakenly writes “satisfy Juno” instead of Elektra.)
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 6] Elektra lässt bei der Schneiderin Juno aus ihrer Seide ein Kleid fertigen (Dezember). Im Februar verkauft Juno das Kleid um 1.500 an Livia und täuscht Elektra mit einem angeblichen Diebstahl. Livia stirbt im April; ihre ahnungslose Erbin Cleo hat das Kleid ab Mai über ein Jahr im Schrank. Im August des Folgejahres verkauft und übergibt Cleo es um 250 an Melitta, die es im Oktober zu einem Flickenteppich verarbeitet. Besitz und Eigentum im (a) Januar, (b) März, (c) Juli des Folgejahres, (d) Oktober?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 8] Felix lends Titius a team of horses. Titius needs money and gives the horses to the money-lender Nastes as a pledge. (a) Possession before and after the pledging? (b) Which action does Felix have against Nastes — does Nastes have any pleas?
cards.back:
(a) Before: Titius detentor (loan for use), Felix mediate proprietary possessor. Titius' mere inner intention changes nothing; by the pledging (an external act with intent to enrich himself) he commits FURTUM → Felix loses possession; as pledgee, Nastes has natural possession (for Titius as pledger).
(b) REI VINDICATIO against Nastes — he is the proper defendant according to Ulpian (FACULTAS RESTITUENDI) as well as according to Pegasus (pledgees are protected by interdicts).
• No effective plea: Titius was neither owner nor authorised to dispose → no right of pledge (NEMO PLUS IURIS …), hence no EXCEPTIO PIGNERATICIA. Nastes is left with the ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM CONTRARIA against Titius; Felix additionally has the ACTIO FURTI against Titius.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 8] Felix leiht Titius ein Pferdegespann. Titius braucht Geld und übergibt die Pferde dem Geldverleiher Nastes als Pfand. (a) Besitzlage vor und nach der Verpfändung? (b) Welche Klage hat Felix gegen Nastes — hat Nastes Einreden?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 10] Felix has granted Tiro a right of way (ITER). Tiro sells and delivers his land to Crassus, who relies on the right of way and drives cattle across Felix's field. (a) Legal nature and criteria of the right of way? (b) What may Crassus do? (c) How does Felix defend himself?
cards.back:
(a) Rustic praedial servitude: limited right in rem of the respective owner of the dominant land; tied to the land; criteria VICINITAS and UTILITAS; considerate exercise (CIVILITER).
(b) The right passed to Crassus together with the land. ITER = only walking/riding — driving cattle would be ACTUS; no unilateral extension.
(c) ACTIO NEGATORIA against the claim to a right to drive cattle (declaration + restoration), if need be fencing off against the excess.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 10] Felix hat Tiro ein Wegerecht (ITER) eingeräumt. Tiro verkauft und übergibt sein Grundstück an Crassus, der sich auf das Wegerecht beruft und Vieh über Felix' Feld treibt. (a) Rechtsnatur und Kriterien des Wegerechts? (b) Was darf Crassus? (c) Wie wehrt sich Felix?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 13] Thea pledges her slave Pamphilus to Aratos (150). Then she borrows 200 from Brontes and pledges him — pointing out Aratos' pledge — the SUPERFLUUM. A year later Aratos lends a further 100 and receives “the same security as for the first loan”. (a) Rank of the three rights of pledge? (b) How much must Brontes pay to avert Aratos' enforcement?
cards.back:
(a) 1. Aratos (150), 2. Brontes (200, in the surplus after Aratos' FIRST claim), 3. Aratos (100) — PRIOR TEMPORE, POTIOR IURE; cf Tryphoninus D 20.4.20.
(b) 150 — with the IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI he only has to pay off the senior claim; Aratos' second claim (100) is junior.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 13] Thea verpfändet ihren Sklaven Pamphilus an Aratos (150). Dann leiht sie 200 von Brontes und verpfändet ihm — unter Hinweis auf Aratos' Pfand — das SUPERFLUUM. Ein Jahr später leiht Aratos weitere 100 und erhält „dieselbe Sicherheit wie beim ersten Darlehen“. (a) Rang der drei Pfandrechte? (b) Wie viel muss Brontes zahlen, um Aratos' Verwertung abzuwenden?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 17] Leo grants Titius (loan 1.000) a non-possessory pledge in two marble statues (small 600, large 800). (a) Titius permits the sale — the small one for at least 700, the large one for at least 900; Leo sells both to Helena for 800 each and delivers them. (b) One of Leo's slaves inadvertently works the large statue into a column (400); Leo does not pay. What can Titius do?
cards.back:
(a) Small statue: condition met (800 ≥ 700) → waiver, Helena acquires free of the pledge. Large statue: 800 < 900 → agreement breached, no waiver (Marcianus D 20.6.8.14) → Titius keeps the right of pledge and can pursue it with the VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against Helena (whether Helena acquires ownership at all, or burdened ownership, depends on whether Leo acted knowingly — as a FUR).
(b) The column is an ALIUD (SPECIFICATIO) → the right of pledge in the large statue terminates (D 13.7.18.3). Because of INDIVISA EST PIGNORIS CAUSA, the small statue is liable for the entire debt → VINDICATIO PIGNORIS and enforcement; the rest as a personal claim against Leo.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 17] Leo verpfändet Titius (Darlehen 1.000) besitzlos zwei Marmorstatuen (klein 600, groß 800). (a) Titius erlaubt den Verkauf — die kleine um mindestens 700, die große um mindestens 900; Leo verkauft beide um je 800 an Helena und übergibt sie. (b) Ein Sklave Leos verarbeitet versehentlich die große Statue zu einer Säule (400); Leo zahlt nicht. Was kann Titius tun?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 18] In February 130 Irene borrows Julia's ruby necklace and acquires a similar glass-bead necklace. In June 130 she mistakenly returns the glass necklace. In October 131 she gives the ruby necklace as a gift to the unsuspecting Pius, who loses it; in summer 132 Hermes has it, who wants to return it but does not know to whom. Legal situation (a) of the ruby necklace with Hermes, (b) of the glass necklace with Julia — actions?
cards.back:
(a) Ruby necklace: Julia remains owner. No FURTUM by Irene (mistake) → RES HABILIS; Pius, in good faith and with gift as title, acquired possession capable of usucaption, but lost it before a year had passed → no usucaption. Hermes does not want the necklace for himself (not a FUR); he holds it for the person entitled.
• Julia: REI VINDICATIO against Hermes (according to Ulpian also against the mere holder with FACULTAS RESTITUENDI). Pius: ACTIO PUBLICIANA — successful against Hermes, failing against Julia because of the EXCEPTIO IUSTI DOMINII.
(b) Glass necklace: Irene remains owner — the return was meant to concern the ruby necklace; for the glass necklace there is no causa. Julia is a bona fide possessor; usucaption at most if a putative title is recognised (PRO SUO, disputed) → Irene: REI VINDICATIO against Julia.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 18] Irene leiht im Februar 130 Julias Rubinkette und erwirbt eine ähnliche Glasperlenkette. Im Juni 130 gibt sie versehentlich die Glaskette zurück. Im Oktober 131 schenkt sie die Rubinkette dem ahnungslosen Pius, der sie verliert; im Sommer 132 hat sie Hermes, der sie zurückgeben will, aber nicht weiß, wem. Rechtslage (a) zur Rubinkette bei Hermes, (b) zur Glaskette bei Julia — Klagen?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 19] Ago leases two fields from Vibia and sows wheat and barley. In summer he cuts the wheat and stores it in a makeshift wooden hut on the field. When he wants to harvest the barley, barley and wheat are gone: Marcus, Vibia's divorced husband, has taken everything. Claims (a) concerning the wheat, (b) concerning the barley?
cards.back:
(a) Wheat: Ago has acquired ownership of it by PERCEPTIO (cutting, bringing in) → REI VINDICATIO or CONDICTIO FURTIVA against Marcus, plus ACTIO FURTI. (While growing, the crop belonged to the landowner as SATIO.)
(b) Barley: separated by Marcus → property of Vibia (owner of the mother object) → only Vibia: CONDICTIO FURTIVA/REI VINDICATIO + ACTIO FURTI; Ago can compel Vibia to take action by the ACTIO CONDUCTI (Example 26).
• The movable hut remains Ago's property (no foundation).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 19] Ago pachtet von Vibia zwei Felder und sät Weizen und Gerste. Im Sommer schneidet er den Weizen und lagert ihn in einer behelfsmäßigen Holzhütte auf dem Feld. Als er die Gerste ernten will, sind Gerste und Weizen weg: Marcus, Vibias geschiedener Mann, hat alles genommen. Ansprüche (a) wegen des Weizens, (b) wegen der Gerste?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 20] Without authority, Helena sells and delivers a plot of land to the bona fide Carus. Before winter Carus plants 40 pear trees (10 each). In April five have withered. In June Carus puts up a tent. In summer the owner Dexter demands the land; Carus engages in the proceedings. Legal position (a) of Dexter, (b) of Carus — remedies, extent?
cards.back:
(a) Dexter is owner (usucaption — 2 years — not completed) → REI VINDICATIO against the possessor Carus: land including the rooted trees (IMPLANTATIO, SUPERFICIES SOLO CEDIT); fruits from LITIS CONTESTATIO; otherwise condemnation QUANTI EA RES ERIT.
(b) Carus (in good faith): EXCEPTIO DOLI → retention until his expenses are reimbursed, at most to the extent of the increase in value (Celsus D 6.1.38) — the withered trees do not increase the value (so at most 35 × 10 = 350). The tent is movable and remains his property.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 20] Helena verkauft und übergibt unbefugt ein Grundstück an den gutgläubigen Carus. Vor dem Winter pflanzt Carus 40 Birnbäume (je 10). Im April sind fünf verdorrt. Im Juni stellt Carus ein Zelt auf. Im Sommer verlangt Eigentümer Dexter das Grundstück; Carus lässt sich auf den Prozess ein. Rechtsstellung (a) Dexters, (b) des Carus — Rechtsbehelfe, Umfang?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 21] Publius, put under tutelage as a PRODIGUS, sells and delivers land to Gorgias; Gorgias learns of the incapacitation only two days after delivery. He then builds a villa for 100.000 (increase in value 80.000). Publius' curator learns of this 13 months after delivery and demands the land back. Will he prevail?
cards.back:
Yes.
• No derivative acquisition: the PRODIGUS cannot dispose without his curator.
• USUCAPIO: Gorgias was in good faith on acquisition (later knowledge does no harm — MALA FIDES SUPERVENIENS NON NOCET; when acquiring from a PRODIGUS, good faith suffices in place of a valid title), but land → 2 years; not completed after 13 months → REI VINDICATIO by the curator.
• Gorgias built only AFTER he knew → no EXCEPTIO DOLI for reimbursement, only IUS TOLLENDI (Ulpian (Iulianus) D 6.1.37, Case 129).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 21] Der als PRODIGUS entmündigte Publius verkauft und übergibt Gorgias ein Grundstück; Gorgias erfährt erst zwei Tage nach der Übergabe von der Entmündigung. Danach baut er eine Villa um 100.000 (Wertsteigerung 80.000). Publius' Kurator erfährt 13 Monate nach der Übergabe davon und verlangt das Grundstück heraus. Setzt er sich durch?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 23] Seius promises Cato his ship as a pledge for a loan of 100.000 but does not deliver it. After storm damage he commissions Maevia to repair it; she demands the ship as a pledge for her fee, and Seius brings it to her shipyard. Seius can pay neither the 50.000 repair costs nor Cato's loan. Can Cato demand the ship from Maevia? How can Maevia keep it?
cards.back:
• Cato has a valid non-possessory pledge (claim + ownership + CONVENTIO PIGNORIS; delivery unnecessary) and the older rank → VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against Maevia; he would overcome her EXCEPTIO REI SIBI QUOQUE PIGNERATAE with the REPLICATIO REI SIBI ANTE PIGNERATAE.
• But: exception to the principle of priority — claim for the preservation/restoration of the pledged thing (Ulpian D 20.4.5: credit for repairing a pledged ship) → Maevia's pledge ranks first; she can keep the ship (and enforce).
• Cato can pay her off (IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI) in order to enforce himself.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 23] Seius verspricht Cato sein Schiff als Pfand für ein Darlehen von 100.000, übergibt es aber nicht. Nach einem Sturmschaden beauftragt er Maevia mit der Reparatur; sie verlangt das Schiff als Pfand für ihren Lohn, Seius bringt es in ihre Werft. Seius kann weder die 50.000 Reparaturkosten noch Catos Darlehen zahlen. Kann Cato das Schiff von Maevia verlangen? Wie kann Maevia es behalten?

cards.topic: 15.12. Klausur 2 — Textbook exam cases (acquiring ownership III, protection, pledge)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 24] On 1 February Ago gives the horse Kalypso to Curio as a gift. On 1 March Curio pledges it to Kassandra (rent debt 10.000), on 1 May to Sophia (loan 20.000). Curio pays Kassandra 8.000 and Sophia nothing, although the debt is due. (a) Ago dies; his heir Agathon demands the horse from Curio. (b) How does Sophia obtain (natural) possession — and what if Kassandra then demands that it be handed over?
cards.back:
(a) No. Gift + TRADITIO of a RES MANCIPI → Curio is bonitarian owner; Ago and his heir have only the NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM (year of usucaption not yet over). Against Agathon's REI VINDICATIO: EXCEPTIO DOLI (in the case of a sale it would be the EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE).
• Both rights of pledge are valid — bonitarian ownership suffices for pledging.
(b) Sophia: VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against Curio (due, unpaid). If Kassandra (rank 1, 2.000 outstanding) then sues Sophia: EXCEPTIO REI SIBI QUOQUE PIGNERATAE → REPLICATIO REI SIBI ANTE PIGNERATAE → Kassandra wins. Sophia can pay Kassandra off with 2.000 (IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 24] Ago schenkt am 1.2. Curio das Pferd Kalypso. Am 1.3. verpfändet Curio es Kassandra (Mietschuld 10.000), am 1.5. Sophia (Darlehen 20.000). Curio zahlt Kassandra 8.000, Sophia nichts trotz Fälligkeit. (a) Ago stirbt; sein Erbe Agathon verlangt das Pferd von Curio. (b) Wie erlangt Sophia (natürlichen) Besitz — und was, wenn danach Kassandra Herausgabe verlangt?
